articles.title: All 14 Indians Aboard Yacht Off Yemen Reported Safe Around Hodeidah

articles.title: BJP Cites Fox News Report to Accuse Congress of Links to Global Protest Network

articles.nri_angle: Sheetla Mata Temple draws large Navratri crowds, and the barricade failure raises crowd and traffic safety questions familiar to diaspora families visiting major temples during festivals in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kolkata Pandal Stampede Toll Rises to 19, High Court Judge to Lead Probe
articles.excerpt: Two more deaths were confirmed in the Chorbagan crush, taking the toll to 19 including 13 women and a child, as West Bengal sought a judge-led SIT and announced Rs 25 lakh for each bereaved family.
articles.nri_angle: Durga Puja is celebrated by Bengali diaspora communities worldwide, and the safety review in Kolkata will be closely watched by organisers of large festival gatherings abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kolkata Durga Puja Pandal Crush Kills at Least 17, Organisers Detained
articles.excerpt: A rain-driven surge at the exit gate of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin pandal on Saturday evening killed at least 17 people and injured 25, with later reports putting the toll at 19; police detained organisers and ordered a forensic probe.
articles.image_caption: Crowds gather in the rain outside the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening. At least 17 people were killed in a crush at the pandal exit gate, and police have detained the organisers for questioning.
articles.nri_angle: Durga Puja is Kolkata's biggest festival and many diaspora families have relatives pandal-hopping this week; the article carries the state helpline (18003455678), hospital and compensation details families abroad may need.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dasara Rush Chokes Hyderabad-Vijayawada Highway as Queues Build at Pantangi Toll
articles.excerpt: Festival traffic, a school holiday through October 22 and unfinished flyover work at Choutuppal combined to slow NH-65 to 20-40 minutes on short service-road stretches.
articles.image_caption: Traffic on National Highway 65 between Hyderabad and Vijayawada, where Dasara queues built at the Pantangi toll plaza (file photo).
articles.nri_angle: Festival travel conditions on the corridor many diaspora families use when visiting Hyderabad and Andhra Pradesh at Dasara.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Durgashtami; Saddula Bathukamma diversions in Hyderabad
Vijayadashami; APSRTC return-phase special buses begin

articles.title: Unseasonal Rain Is Extending India's Dengue, Malaria and Flood-Disease Season
articles.excerpt: Rainfall above roughly 100 mm a month lifts dengue risk toward 2.3 times baseline, mosquitoes are colonising hill districts, and leptospirosis follows every flood.
articles.nri_angle: Families in India face a longer disease season after unseasonal rain; the precautions are concrete and household-level.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's 9.1% Pay Hikes Hide a Widening Split Over AI Skills, Aon Finds
articles.excerpt: Aon's survey of 1,200+ employers projects average hikes of 9.1% for 2027, but 37% of firms plan 10% or more while a quarter — including much of IT services — stay under 8% as AI-role premiums jump about 10%.
articles.image_caption: Bengaluru (file photo). Aon found India's 9.1% pay hikes mask a widening split over AI skills.
articles.nri_angle: The AI-skill premium reshaping India Inc pay — NBFCs at 10.1% versus IT services at 6.6% — directly affects NRI professionals weighing return-to-India offers and GCC roles.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FSSAI Proposes Ban on Added Sugars in Infant Food for Babies Under Six Months
articles.excerpt: A draft amendment published on October 16 would bar adding sucrose and fructose to products for infants up to six months, with 60 days for public comment before the rules can be finalised.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora parents who buy Indian-made infant food should note the ban is still a draft — sucrose and fructose remain permitted within limits until final rules are notified, so ingredient lists are the check that matters today.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi's AQI Leaps From 65 to 216 in a Day as Calm Weather Traps Pollution
articles.excerpt: Friday's rain briefly gave the capital satisfactory air. With the IMD forecasting dry, still days ahead, the winter pollution season has arrived early — and GRAP Stage 1 is already in force.
articles.image_caption: South Block is engulfed in a layer of smog in New Delhi. Delhi's AQI jumped from 65 to 216 in a day as dry, calm weather trapped pollutants over the capital.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families flying into Delhi for Diwali face AQI swings from 65 to 216 within a day; morning AQI checks and masks for sensitive travellers are now part of the trip.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: LK Advani, 98, Admitted to Delhi Hospital With Chest Infection, Condition Stable
articles.excerpt: The former deputy prime minister was brought to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital on Friday evening and is under observation in the pulmonary department. It is his third hospital admission in under two years.
articles.image_caption: L. K. Advani, the former deputy prime minister and BJP founding figure admitted to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital in Delhi with a chest infection.
articles.nri_angle: Advani is a towering figure for a generation of Indians at home and abroad who followed the BJP's rise; his health is followed closely across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Dead, Six Injured as Reactor Blast Rocks Bharuch Pharma Plant in Gujarat
articles.excerpt: A reactor failed during a hydrogenation process at a pharmaceutical unit in the Saykha GIDC area of Vagra, leaking methylene dichloride gas. Officials have opened an investigation and no cause has been established.
articles.image_caption: An injured person is loaded into an ambulance at night while medical staff and bystanders assist. The reactor blast at the Bharuch pharmaceutical plant killed five people and injured six, according to India Today.
articles.nri_angle: Bharuch's chemical belt is a major employer for Gujarati families in India and a region many in the diaspora come from; recurring fatal plant accidents there are a standing safety concern.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 24 Indian Seafarers Safe After Tankers Hit in Hormuz and Off Romania, Minister Says
articles.excerpt: Crude tanker MT ST 3, with 15 Indian crew, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 16; chemical tanker Yara J, with nine Indians aboard, was hit by a drone at Sulina Anchorage on October 14. No casualties on either vessel.
articles.nri_angle: India supplies a large share of the world's merchant crews; every attack on commercial shipping in the Gulf or Black Sea puts Indian families on shore on alert.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Antibiotic Crisis Is a Failure of Hospital Care, Not Just Overuse
articles.excerpt: An ICMR study of 159,336 patients found most infections from four major bacteria were carbapenem-resistant, with bloodstream mortality up to 50.8% and treatment costs roughly double.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs arranging hospital care for parents in India should ask about culture testing and stewardship, as resistant infections there now carry up to 50.8% bloodstream mortality.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
